disclaimer: Every number here is SIMULATED: a model fitted to the hospital's published aggregates, not its operational data. Differences are paired on the same simulated patients; intervals are 95% Student-t over seeds.

protocol.ci: 95% Student-t interval of the mean paired difference over seeds

reward.value_definition: reward_value_per_day = change in reward per hour x cost scale x 24: the dollars of daily cost the objective would trade for the unit (its own cost already netted off). An exchange rate set by the chosen weights, not cash.
reward.definition: reward per hour = -sum_k w_k * term_k / scale_k; scale_k = this run's baseline mean per hour on normal_week (floored; revenue uses the cost scale). Re-score with any weights from `terms_seeds` (raw per-hour term differences per seed) without re-simulating.
reward.scale_source: baseline of this run, normal_week, 32 seeds x 30 days

flow_index.definition: weighted sum of (metric / its baseline) over these metrics; `flow_index_pct` is the change in percent of the baseline index, positive = worse flow

location.note: The simulator walks every patient of a bay class over the same distance (class centroid to zone centroid), so all bays of a class have the same simulated value. These are the geometric differences it ignores: seconds a single walk in plus one leg to CT would gain or lose for this bay against its class centroid. Geometry only, not a simulated outcome.

identifiability: Providers of a role are interchangeable in the model: a named provider has the value of one provider on that shift. The model has no individual skill, speed or specialty, so no per-person differences are reported.
A 'provider' is costed at the blended wage of the attending / resident / APP mix; the model does not move patients differently by role (except the fast-track provider's productivity).

Bays of a class differ only by position, and the simulator walks patients between zone centroids, so every bay of a class has the same simulated value. `location` gives the per-bay distances it ignores.
A ward bed is one bed of the pooled inpatient capacity the ED admits to (ward, step-down and ICU rooms pooled); beds are not distinguished.
Removing a ward bed also changes the starting census (the pool starts at a fixed occupancy share), so its effect includes that.
Staff the model holds constant (technicians, registration, pharmacist, transport, EVS, charge nurse) cannot be removed in it and have no marginal value here.
Scanner purchase price and bay construction cost are capital, outside the daily figures.

Nurses constrain the model only through a cap on staffed spaces per nurse and through care minutes; the nurse and provider head-counts are calibration parameters fitted to public aggregates, not the hospital's roster. 'Slack' and 'needed' describe that fitted model.

The dollar 'value to the objective' is the reward change at the objective's own exchange rate between cost and waiting, walk-outs, safety and boarding. It moves with the weights; it is not cash. Margin alone is the cash figure, and in this cost model slower care can raise it (more admissions, each booked as revenue).

normal_week.rule: worth adding: the balanced reward rises with a 95% interval above zero. needed: removing it makes a flow or safety metric worse (interval above zero and not inside the equivalence margin) and lowers the balanced reward (interval below zero). slack: removing it saves money (interval above zero), every flow and safety metric's interval stays inside its equivalence margin, i.e. it is shown to get at most negligibly worse (margin: 2% of baseline for waits, stay, walk-outs and boarding; 5% for rare safety events), and the balanced reward does not measurably fall. Anything else is not shown either way.
